outcomeNote: mishna; R' Yosei's statement is explained in the gemara

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁהָלְכָה אִשְׁתּוֹ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם, בָּאוּ וְאָמְרוּ לוֹ ״מֵתָה אִשְׁתְּךָ״, וְנָשָׂא אֶת אֲחוֹתָהּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּאת אִשְׁתּוֹ — מוּתֶּרֶת לַחְזוֹר
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In the case of «one whose wife went overseas» and people «came and told him: Your wife is dead, and he married her sister, and afterward his wife came» back from overseas, the original wife «is permitted to return»

segments.he: לוֹ. וּמוּתָּר בִּקְרוֹבוֹת שְׁנִיָּה, וּשְׁנִיָּה מוּתֶּרֶת בִּקְרוֹבָיו. וְאִם מֵתָה רִאשׁוֹנָה — מוּתָּר בַּשְּׁנִיָּה.
segments.en: «to him,» as his erroneous marriage to her sister is considered licentious sexual relations, and one who has intercourse with his wife’s relatives has not rendered his first wife forbidden to himself. «And he is permitted to the relatives of the second» woman, e.g., her daughter, «and» this «second» woman «is permitted to his relatives,» e.g., his son, as the marriage was entirely invalid. «And if the first» woman «died» he is «permitted to the second» woman, despite the fact that he has already engaged in forbidden relations with her.

segments.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מֵתָה אִשְׁתּוֹ, וְנָשָׂא אֶת אֲחוֹתָהּ. וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמְרוּ לוֹ: קַיֶּימֶת הָיְתָה, וּמֵתָה. הַוָּלָד רִאשׁוֹן — מַמְזֵר, וְהָאַחֲרוֹן — אֵין מַמְזֵר. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל שֶׁפּוֹסֵל עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים — פּוֹסֵל עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ, וְכֹל שֶׁאֵין פּוֹסֵל עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים — אֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵל עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ.
segments.en: If «they said to him» that «his wife is dead, and he married her sister, and afterward they said to him» that «she was alive» when he married the sister «and» only later «died,» in this case «the first child,» born to the sister while his wife was still alive, is «a mamzer,» as he was born from the union of a man and his sister-in-law, «and the last one is not a mamzer. Rabbi Yosei says: Whoever disqualifies others» also «disqualifies himself, and whoever does not disqualify others does not disqualify himself» either. Rabbi Yosei’s obscure statement will be explained by the Gemara.

moves.summary: wife returns: permitted to him; he permitted to the second's relatives; permitted to the second after the first dies
if the wife was alive at the marriage and then died, the first child is a mamzer and the later one not
R' Yosei: whoever disqualifies through others disqualifies through himself
moves.about: the principle for when a man's mistaken marriage to his wife's sister renders his own wife forbidden (whoever disqualifies others disqualifies himself)

whoever disqualifies through others disqualifies through himself, and whoever does not, does not
